title: Supported Liquid Extraction and Measurement of 18 Steroids in Plasma by LC-MS/MS
author: Denham, Simpson, et al.

steps.title: Prepare 11‑dehydrocorticosterone stock
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 2 mg of 11‑dehydrocorticosterone into a glass vial, add methanol (HPLC grade) to bring the volume to 2 mL, mix thoroughly and label the solution as a 1 mg · mL⁻¹ stock.

steps.title: Make 15‑steroid mix solution
steps.instruction: Combine the following steroid stock solutions (all at 1 mg · mL⁻¹ unless otherwise noted) with methanol to a final volume of 1000 µL (570 µL methanol) as listed in Table 2.1: P4 100 µL, B 50 µL, DHEA 50 µL, T 20 µL, A4 10 µL, 17α‑OHP 5 µL, A 5 µL, S 5 µL, DHT 5 µL, E2 25 µL, E1 15 µL, E3 31 µL, 21‑DF 50 µL, 11‑DOC 50 µL, Aldo 50 µL. Vortex to mix and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standard stocks
steps.instruction: Using the 15‑steroid mix from the previous step, prepare the following calibration mixes (final volume 1000 µL each) with the indicated certified reference standards and methanol: 100 Mix – 100 µL 1 mg · mL⁻¹ F*, 50 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ E, 10 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ P5, 10 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ 17OHP5, add methanol to 1000 µL; 10 Mix – 100 µL of 100 Mix diluted with 900 µL methanol; 1 Mix – 100 µL of 10 Mix diluted with 900 µL methanol; 0.1 Mix – 100 µL of 1 Mix diluted with 900 µL methanol. Store all dilutions at –20 °C and colour‑code the vials for easy identification.

steps.title: Prepare working internal standard (WIS)
steps.instruction: First prepare the Internal Standard Mix (Int Std Mix) by adding the following to a glass vial: 125 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ 13C3‑E*, 100 µL 10 µg · mL⁻¹ 13C3‑B*, 25 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ d9‑P*, 10 µL each of 100 µg · mL⁻¹ d5‑S*, d8‑21DF*, 13C3‑T*, 13C3‑A4*, 13C3‑DHT*, d8‑17OHP4*, 13C2,d2‑P5*, d8‑Aldo*, 13C3‑E2*, 13C3‑E1*, 13C3‑E3*; add methanol to 1000 µL. Then make the final WIS: for a single 96‑well plate use 2 mL total – add 20 µL Int Std Mix, 15 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ 13C3‑F*, 10 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ d5‑DHEA to reach 2 mL with methanol; for multiple plates use 10 mL total – add 100 µL Int Std Mix, 125 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ 13C3‑F*, 50 µL 100 µg · mL⁻¹ d5‑DHEA and bring to 10 mL with methanol. Store WIS at –20 °C.

steps.title: Design electronic 96‑well plate map
steps.instruction: Using the supplied Excel template (Supplementary S1), create a plate map for each batch (≤ 74 samples) that includes double blanks, solvent blanks, the calibration standards (0.1 Mix, 1 Mix, 10 Mix), six quality controls (Chromsystems Panel 1 & 2, levels I‑III), and the samples. Save the map for later import into the mass‑spectrometer software.

steps.title: Create and save batch sequence in MS software
steps.instruction: Import the electronic plate map into the instrument control software (e.g., Analyst), verify that the injection order is column‑wise, and save the sequence file for later use.

steps.title: Defrost samples and prepare collection plate
steps.instruction: Thaw plasma or serum samples, centrifuge if needed, then label a 96‑well 2 mL deep‑well collection plate (Biotage). According to the plate map, add 200 µL water to each blank well of the collection plate.

steps.title: Add calibration standards to plate
steps.instruction: Following Table 2.4 and the column‑wise plate map, pipette the specified volumes of Working IS (WIS) and calibration standard stock into each calibration well, then add water to bring the total volume to 200 µL. Example for 0.1 Mix (STD 0): add 200 µL WIS, 0 µL STD, 0 µL water; for 0.1 Mix (STD 1): add 5 µL 0.1 Mix, 195 µL WIS, 0 µL water; continue for all 12 calibration points as listed in Table 2.4.

steps.title: Add quality controls
steps.instruction: Aliquot 200 µL of each of the six QC materials into the wells designated for QCs according to the plate map.

steps.title: Add plasma samples
steps.instruction: Pipette 200 µL of each thawed plasma (or serum) sample into its assigned ‘sample’ well as defined by the plate map.

steps.title: Add WIS to samples and shake
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of the prepared WIS to every well except the double blank and solvent blank wells. Seal the plate, place it on a ThermoPlate shaker set to 600 rpm for 5 min, then transfer the plate to the Extrahera liquid‑handling robot.

steps.title: Program robot for SLE400+ extraction
steps.instruction: Program the robot to: 1) dispense 200 µL of 0.1 % formic acid (aq) into each well, wait 5 min; 2) add 600 µL of 98:2 dichloromethane:isopropanol to each well of the SLE400+ plate; 3) collect eluate under positive pressure into the deep‑well collection plate; 4) repeat steps 2–3 two more times so that each well receives a total of 1.8 mL eluate.

steps.title: Dry down eluates
steps.instruction: Transfer the deep‑well collection plate to a nitrogen evaporator, dry the samples to completeness under a stream of nitrogen at 40 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend dried extracts
steps.instruction: Add 80 µL of 70:30 water:methanol to each well, seal the plate and shake on a ThermoShaker at 600 rpm for 10 min to ensure complete resuspension.

steps.title: Set up LC‑MS/MS chromatography
steps.instruction: Configure the UPLC (I‑Class Acquity or equivalent) with a Kinetex C18 column (2.1 × 150 mm, 2.6 µm) equipped with a KrudKatcher Ultra In‑Line Filter (0.5 µm). Use mobile phase A: water + 50 µM ammonium fluoride; mobile phase B: methanol + 50 µM ammonium fluoride. Set flow = 0.3 mL · min⁻¹, column temperature = 50 °C, injection volume = 20 µL. Gradient: 0–2 min 50 % B, 2–8 min linear to 100 % B, 8–10 min hold 100 % B, 10–10.1 min return to 50 % B, re‑equilibrate 4.9 min. Divert flow to waste from 0–2 min and 11–16 min.

steps.title: Set up mass spectrometer parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the QTrap 6500+ (or equivalent) in Analyst 1.7.1 for electrospray ionisation with polarity switching. Source temperature = 600 °C, IonSpray voltage = +5.5 kV/‑4.5 kV, curtain gas = 30 psi, GS1 = 40 psi, GS2 = 60 psi. Acquire data in unit resolution (0.7 m/z FWHM) using the MRM transitions listed in Tables 2.5 and 2.6 for each analyte and its isotopically labelled internal standard.

steps.title: Set up batch analysis in software
steps.instruction: Import the experimental plate map (Excel) into the mass‑spectrometer control software, create a batch sequence that follows the column‑wise injection order, and include a system‑suitability injection (Std 2) before the first sample. Run the sequence: solvent blank → double blank → calibration curve → double blanks → Panel 1 QCs → unknown samples → Panel 2 QCs → solvent blank. After acquisition, evaluate retention times, calibration linearity, QC accuracy, and check for interfering peaks.
